1. Baseline (Julia): the register from the difficulty baseline card. One sheet with two tabs, Tickets and Rules in force, so we tune from what players have and not from what we remember.

Tiers -2 to +2 per level (ZOM-42); tier 0 is the default version of each level.

Starting tier: average CPM over the first 10 levels; 90 or more starts you on tier 1, everyone else on tier 0.

Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm Two things I left out of the mail this morning.

1. The level editor (Assets/Scripts/LevelEditor and the LevelDesigner panels), anything in an Editor folder and the debug menu (Assets/Scripts/Debug) are stripped before we ship to players on iOS and Android. A ticket whose changes are only level editor or debug tooling never reached players, Done or not.

2. For the rules tab: the starting tier check in the code is cpm > 90, not >= 90, and it runs when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted, not after 10 levels cleared. ZOM-199 says >= 90 after the first 10 levels, but the code never changed from the original spec, so 90 exactly stays on tier 0.

Blake

{"result":"{\"id\": \"ZOM-42\", \"uuid\": null, \"identifier\": \"ZOM-42\", \"number\": 42, \"title\": \"Dynamic Difficulty\", \"description\": \"# **Part 1:**\\n\\nAllow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)\\n\\nWhat's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.\\n\\n* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)\\n\\nWhat's not identical in the tiers:\\n\\n* Quantity of the items\\n* Quantity of the monsters\\n* Pre-warm period\\n\\nPlayers starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win streak:\\n\\n1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)\\n2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.\\n\\nPromotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.\\n2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player\\n3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this \\\"early exit\\\" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.\\n\\nDemotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:\\n\\n1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.\\n2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.\\n\\nPlease note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.\\n\\nThis also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.\\n\\nA losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.\\n\\n# **Part 2: Future expansion**\\n\\nIf a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:\\n\\nMonster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with\\n\\nPunk A | Punk B\\n\\nPunk B | Punk C\\n\\nPunk C | Punk D\\n\\nPunk D | Brute A\\n\\nBoss 1 | Boss 3\\n\\nBoss 2 | Boss 4\\n\\nBoss 10 | Boss 10\\n\\nIf the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.\\n\\nThe other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster \\\"rank\\\" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the \\\"next rank\\\" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:\\nPunk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C\\n\\nThen Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.\\n\\nThis will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. This will also prevent us from overcrowding the level with simply too many monsters.\", \"priority\": {\"value\": 1, \"name\": \"Urgent\"}, \"estimate\": null, \"url\": \"https://linear.app/harmonygames/issue/ZOM-42/dynamic-difficulty\", \"gitBranchName\": \"julialawson/zom-42-dynamic-difficulty\", \"createdAt\": \"2025-04-21T16:28:42Z\", \"updatedAt\": \"2025-05-31T02:54:30Z\", \"archivedAt\": null, \"completedAt\": \"2025-05-30T22:06:46Z\", \"startedAt\": \"2025-05-23T15:05:35Z\", \"canceledAt\": null, \"dueDate\": null, \"status\": \"Done\", \"statusType\": \"completed\", \"labels\": [\"Level Editor\", \"Backend Engineering\"], \"links\": [], \"attachments\": [], \"createdBy\": \"Robert\", \"createdById\": \"usr_Robert\", \"assignee\": \"arthur.blake@harmonygames.co\", \"assigneeId\": \"usr_cc3e90160f490686\", \"project\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"projectId\": \"dbab77c7-f871-4888-abf8-d98b52a41624\", \"team\": \"Zombie Match 3D\", \"teamId\": \"team_ZOM\", \"timeInStatusMinutes\": 177655, \"isArchived\": false, \"stateHistory\": []}"}

{"id": "ZOM-42", "uuid": null, "identifier": "ZOM-42", "number": 42, "title": "Dynamic Difficulty", "description": "# **Part 1:**

Allow level editor to create tiered version of each level. Tier 0 is default. Then we have -2, -1, 0, +1, +2 tiers. (Or more if designer creates it, but each level should have a minimum of these 5 tiers, rest are optional)

What's identical across tiers, this is to ensure code consistency across all tiers and keeping code simplified.

* List of items in the level. (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)
* List of monsters in the level (For lower level tiers we can set qty to 0 to effectively not have any)

What's not identical in the tiers:

* Quantity of the items
* Quantity of the monsters
* Pre-warm period

Players starts at default tier 0, but gets assigned after the first 6-7 levels based on CPM, to be defined later, and gets moved up and down based on certain winning/losing conditions.

Demotion Rules based on win streak:

1. Use CPM data to place player in a starting tier. (1st 10 level avg CPM > 90 (top 20%) moves to tier 1, rest stays in tier 0)
2. Lose 4 in a row, you're demoted.

Promotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Tier -2 is an exception. You promote instantly after 1 win if you're in tier -2.
2. Starting at tier -1, we evaluate UP TO THE MOST RECENT 10 attempts of the player
3. We promote if if win rate is 80% or higher. This means we constantly look at the last 10 games played, if at any time win rate is 80%+, we promote. This also means it is possible to be promoted by simply winning 8 games in a row, without playing the full 10 games. We call this "early exit" because you're mathematically guaranteed to win 80%.

Demotion Rules based on win record of last 10 attempts:

1. Similar to promotion rules, we demote someone when their win rate for up to the last 10 games is 50% or lower.
2. Early exits is also possible. Meaning that if you manage to avoid the 4 losing streak demotion, you can still get demoted by doing LLLWLL or LWLWLLL or LLWLLL, these are some cases where you didn't play the full 10 games, but is mathematically guaranteed to finish at 50% or lower win rate.

Please note that every time a promotion/demotion happens, the record is reset and we start at 0 games played.

This also means that with a win rate of 60 or 70%, the player does not get promoted or demoted.

A losing streak of 4 games in a row can still trigger at any time, regardless of whatever record. But a demotion from this will still reset the game record for the win rate evaluation.

# **Part 2: Future expansion**

If a player manages to reach the highest tier difficulty consistently, we will implement an auto tier+ system. What this is will simply be swapping monsters in the level. Meaning we will first create a dictionary table of how we want to swap monsters. This is a sample of a table:

Monster in Max Tier Difficulty Track | Monsters to replace with

Punk A | Punk B

Punk B | Punk C

Punk C | Punk D

Punk D | Brute A

Boss 1 | Boss 3

Boss 2 | Boss 4

Boss 10 | Boss 10

If the player is winning consistently at a threshold we set, then we run this process *once* when the level starts, replacing all monsters with an upgraded one. If the player continues to excel, then we can run this process *twice* as the level starts. So if this conversion was ran twice, Punk A would first -> Punk B, and that same Punk B -> Punk C, upgraded twice.

The other way to think about this is that we can essentially have monster "rank" for minions and for bosses. And if player manages to approach tier+ 1 then we simply take all the existing monsters and replace them with the "next rank" monster. And we do the same for boss. So let's say we have weakest to strongest minion ranks:
Punk A -> Punk B -> Punk C -> Punk D -> Brute A -> Karen A -> Brute B -> Karen B -> Brute C

Then Tier+1 would move everything up *one* grade. If the player does well, then everything moves up *two grades*. We can continue this for many many tier+ X. In this above sample, a Tier+9 would indicate any regular Punk A in the level, will be replaced by Brute C.

This will prevent us from overloading each level with too many designer made difficulty tiers and monster tracks. values: Rules in force: store builds players have today (iOS 0.3.49, Android 0.3.133, both cut from main on Sep 26)
How it works in the store builds today
Tier 0 is the default version of each level; tiered versions -2, -1, +1, +2 (more if the designer adds them). A level loads the tier version closest to the player's tier.
Code clamps the player tier to -2..+5

Assigned when a player's 10th game ends, wins and losses both counted (not after 10 levels cleared). Average CPM over those 10 games above 90 (cpm > 90) puts them on tier 1; everyone else, including exactly 90, stays on tier 0.
Build, per Blake's Sep 30 reply (TierManager: cpm > 90 at totalGames == 10)
ZOM-199 and Robert's deck say >= 90 after the first 10 levels; the build wins

Starting at tier -1, we evaluate up to the most recent 10 attempts of the player and promote if the win rate is 80% or higher. Early exit: winning 8 in a row promotes without playing the full 10. Tier -2 is an exception: you promote instantly after 1 win. Every promotion or demotion resets the record to 0 games played.

Lose 4 in a row and you're demoted one tier, at any time regardless of record. Also demoted when the win rate for up to the most recent 10 games is 50% or lower (early exit possible, e.g. LLLWLL). A 60-70% win rate neither promotes nor demotes. Every demotion resets the record to 0 games played.

Yes, the level drops: the level the player was on when demoted loads one tier version lower on the retry. After the next win it goes back to normal (the tier version closest to the player's new tier).
Blunder (overfilling the match bar) enrages every monster on the board, including ones still to spawn. Enrage adds walk speed and damage only, no HP. Refill health and push monster back clear enrage.
ZOM-254 replaced by ZOM-282; match3d#401 split speed and damage
Robert's deck still shows the old +25% speed/damage/HP

content.text:
I've built the difficulty register, put it in the ZM Difficulty folder, shared it with everyone on Monday's tuning invite, commented on the tickets his rules called for, and replied to Leonard in the DM.

**The register:** [ZM difficulty baseline register - Oct 6](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1clIng0lY9uNax5VGgZ10frE67fPBrAf-WrvZuk5Ins0/edit) has two tabs, as the session agenda asks:
- **Tickets:** one row per ticket. Columns are ticket, title, Linear state, status, then Robert's three extras (assignee, date marked done in Pacific time, priority), then what replaced it.
- **Rules in force:** starting tier, promotion, demotion, what happens to the level after a demotion, and enrage. It's checked against the live game code, and the per-monster enrage numbers are copied as they stand from your enrage sheet's Live tab.

**What I told Leonard:**
- **Tickets on the list:** 33 — 21 Live, 8 Editor only, 1 Replaced, 3 Not shipped.
- **Replaced:** ZOM-282 replaced ZOM-254 (the Blunder 2.0 enrage boost). It's the only one.
- **Starting tier:** a new player gets it when their 10th game ends, counting wins and losses, not after 10 levels cleared. An average CPM above 90 starts them on tier 1. Everyone else, including exactly 90, starts on tier 0. ZOM-199 and Robert's deck both say "90 or more", but Blake confirmed the build never changed, so the register follows the build.

**Linear comments (14):**
- ZOM-199: what the build actually does.
- ZOM-254: replaced by ZOM-282.
- The 8 Editor only and 3 Not shipped tickets: the change isn't in the store builds.

**Off the list:**
- ZOM-258 (the enraged-monster icon): Leonard's notes say leave it off.
- ZOM-295 and ZOM-312: Blake marked their PRs "not tiers".
- Five tickets without matching titles are on the list because Blake's closing notes start with "tiers:": ZOM-221, 281, 300, 305 and 378.

**Decision for you:** Leonard added three changes after writing the card's rules (a checklist on the card and a notes doc attached to it), and I followed all of them:
- Brian got edit access as well as Robert.
- Arthur got view-only access instead of comment.
- The Editor only and Not shipped tickets got comments, which the card's own rule 6 said not to do.

They're all from Leonard and newer than the card text, but if you'd rather stick to the card as written, the fix is removing those 11 Linear comments and changing Brian and Arthur to commenter.

Three monsters (Mailman, Mayor2, PartyGirl) show as "not copied yet" on the rules tab, because that's how your enrage sheet has them.
